text:
maia: Morning — brief announcement about next week's deploy window. We're adjusting the default canary from 10% to 20% for routes that meet the "stable-fallback" checklist. Goal: detect perf regressions faster without manual intervention.

toni: Can we gate this to only routes with autoscaling enabled? last time a canary spiked backend connections.

maia: yes, autoscaling required. We'll add an automated rollback rule (error_rate > 0.5% for 5m) and require fallback model configured.

raj: Sounds reasonable. What about customer-facing routes during peak hours?

maia: we'll exclude routes marked "critical-sla" by default. If you own a critical route and want extra isolation, add `dedicated_fallback: true` to the route config.

sasha: small ops request: shift weekend quiet window to avoid midweek churn. Proposed temporary window: Sat 18:00 UTC -> Mon 06:00 UTC for next two cycles. emergency exceptions still go through the release-exceptions flow.

toni: exception process reminder: create ticket in #release-exceptions, tag @toni and @sre, include risk, rollback steps, and load projection.

deploy-bot: :loud_sound: Scheduled rollout: canary-defaults/v2024.11 -> Mon 06:00 UTC. Owners: maia, toni. Link: https://console.redwood.example/releases/2024.11

maia: Config snippet we'll publish in the docs page tonight:

```
rollout:
  initial_canary: 0.2
  autoscale_required: true
  monitor:
    error_rate_threshold: 0.005
    window_seconds: 300
  fallback_model: compatible-1.3
  exclude_labels: ["critical-sla"]
```

raj: I'll run a perf sweep on dedicated pools before the rollout. ping me if you want to hold.

sasha: tagging @all-release-owners: if your route will be part of the 20% canary and you need exclusion, DM maia by EOD today.

maia: thanks everyone. we'll post the full route list and docs link by EOD. :thumbsup:
